surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $1.2 billion, about 14% above the preview’s $1.05 billion consensus estimate. The preview expected a modest beat around $1.055 billion, so the reported result was materially stronger.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $245 million, roughly 25% above the preview’s $196 million estimate. Profit also grew faster than revenue, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 21% versus the preview’s 18.6% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 70% year-over-year to $245 million with margin expanding 1.6 percentage points to 21%.”

surprises.description: Equipment adjusted segment EBITDA margin was 17.1%, above the preview’s 15–16.5% range for Q3 and its roughly 15.5% estimate. That is a stronger margin recovery than the preview expected for this key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equipment adjusted segment EBITDA margin surged from 7.1% in Q1 to 17.1% in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs to show 15–16.5%”; “My estimates: ... equipment segment margin ~15.5%.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $780–800 million from the preview’s expected $720–740 million, a $60 million increase at the midpoint. Revenue guidance also rose to $3.9–4.0 billion from $3.8–3.9 billion, rather than being reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, lifting adjusted EBITDA to $780-$800 million (up $60 million at midpoint) and revenue to $3.9-$4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimates: ... FY26 guidance reaffirmed, not raised”; prior guide: “$3.8–3.9B” revenue and “$720–740M” adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: Equipment demand and backlog were much stronger than the preview’s expectation that Q3 orders could look pedestrian and backlog could be roughly flat: equipment backlog reached $8 billion, versus $6.6 billion previously, with $2.2 billion of Q3 equipment orders. Combined backlog and slot reservations also rose to about 19 GW from more than 15 GW last quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equipment order backlog reached a record $8 billion ... with a last-12-month book-to-bill ratio of 3.3x and $2.2 billion in Q3 equipment orders”; “combined backlog and slot reservations rising to ~19 GW from over 15 GW last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 standalone orders could look pedestrian versus Q2’s ... $2.3B, and backlog may read roughly flat”; preview cited “$6.6B equipment backlog” and “>15 GW of backlog plus slot reservations.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that the largest customer’s share of order intake is expected to fall from 41% in 2025 to about 21% in the near-term outlook. The preview did not anticipate this company-specific reduction in customer concentration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The largest customer's order intake share falling from 41% in 2025 to approximately 21% in the near-term outlook.”

surprises.description: Management said Innio has allocated no meaningful volumes to Neo cloud operators and instead works with counterparties that typically have back-to-back contracts. This is a reassuringly limited exposure to data-center credit risk, a concern the preview raised in the context of financing worries around the sector.
surprises.fact_evidence: “It has not allocated any meaningful volumes to Neo cloud operators, working instead with hyperscalers, co-locators, and energy-as-a-service firms that typically have back-to-back contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “a sector-wide unwind of the AI-power trade” and “Meta capex-financing and rate worries.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a higher service-revenue outlook for new installed capacity: more than $50,000 annually per MW, compared with about $30,000 for the existing fleet. The preview discussed service margins but did not set an expectation for this per-MW revenue level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The added installed base [is] expected to generate more than $50,000 in annual service revenue per megawatt (~70% above the ~$30,000 from the existing 44 GW fleet).”

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.1x and approaching the stated medium-term target of below 2x. That provides a favorable balance-sheet update against the preview’s focus on debt and whether the capacity ramp could be self-funded, although the preview did not specify a leverage forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.6x at year-end 2025, approaching the sub-2x medium-term target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “free cash flow and capex” and the capacity ramp’s claim to be “self-funded from operating cash flow,” but did not give a net-leverage expectation.
